qa.e: When the structure of atoms is altered, a lot of energy is released as heat, which is used to make electricity.

qa.q: Which action helps conserve energy?
qa.a: Using public transport instead of private vehicles
qa.e: Public transport carries many people using less fuel per person; 'energy saved is energy produced'.

qa.q: Why is manufacturing called the 'backbone of development'?
qa.a: It modernises agriculture, creates jobs and earns foreign exchange
qa.e: Manufacturing modernises farming, creates secondary and tertiary jobs, reduces poverty and earns foreign exchange through exports.

qa.q: When many industries cluster in a city to share services like banking, transport and labour, the advantages are called:
qa.e: Agglomeration economies are the benefits of industries locating together near an urban centre.

qa.q: Which of these is a basic or key industry?
qa.e: Iron and steel supplies its products to other industries, so it is a basic or key industry; the others are consumer industries.

qa.q: Bajaj Auto and Dabur are examples of which sector?
qa.e: They are owned and operated by individuals or groups, so they are private sector industries.

qa.q: Oil India Ltd is an example of the:
qa.e: Oil India Ltd is jointly run by the state and individuals or firms, so it is in the joint sector.

qa.q: The sugar industry in Maharashtra is a well-known example of the:
qa.e: Many sugar mills in Maharashtra are owned and run by sugarcane growers in cooperatives.

qa.q: Industries are classified as heavy or light on the basis of:
qa.a: Bulk and weight of raw materials and finished goods
qa.e: Heavy industries like iron and steel handle bulky, heavy goods; light industries like electrical goods handle light goods.

qa.q: How do industries help agriculture?
qa.a: By supplying irrigation pumps, fertilisers, pesticides and machines
qa.e: Industries make many farm inputs such as pumps, fertilisers, pesticides, PVC pipes and machines, raising productivity.

qa.q: Which of these is an agro-based industry?
qa.e: Cotton textiles use cotton from farms as raw material; the others use minerals.

qa.q: In which year was the first successful textile mill set up in Mumbai?
qa.e: The first successful textile mill came up in Mumbai in 1854; the first jute mill came a year later, in 1855.

qa.q: Why is the textile industry unique in India?
qa.a: It is self-reliant and complete in the value chain
qa.e: It covers everything from raw material (cotton) to the highest value-added products (garments) within the country.

qa.q: Where was India's first jute mill set up?
qa.e: The first jute mill was set up at Rishra near Kolkata in 1855.

qa.q: Which is NOT a reason for jute mills being located along the Hugli river?
qa.e: Jute mills need raw jute, water, cheap transport, labour and port services — not iron ore.

qa.q: Early cotton mills grew in Maharashtra and Gujarat because of:
qa.a: Raw cotton, market, transport, ports, labour and a moist climate
qa.e: The cotton-growing belt offered raw cotton, markets, transport, ports, labour and a moist climate.

qa.q: In the cotton textile industry, which activity is centralised in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu?
qa.e: Spinning is centralised in these states; weaving is highly decentralised.

qa.q: Khadi helps the economy mainly by:
qa.a: Giving large-scale employment to weavers in their homes
qa.e: Handspun khadi is a cottage industry that gives home-based employment to many weavers.

qa.q: Why is iron and steel called a 'basic industry'?
qa.a: All other industries depend on it for their machinery
qa.e: Heavy, medium and light industries all depend on iron and steel for machinery.

qa.q: Iron ore, coking coal and limestone are required in steel making in roughly what ratio?
qa.e: About 4 parts iron ore, 2 parts coking coal and 1 part limestone are used.

qa.q: Which region has the maximum concentration of iron and steel industries?
qa.e: The Chhotanagpur plateau has iron ore, coal and other raw materials close by, plus cheap labour.

qa.q: Which is the second most important metallurgical industry in India?
qa.e: After iron and steel, aluminium smelting is the second most important metallurgical industry.

qa.q: What are the two main factors for locating an aluminium smelting plant?
qa.a: Regular supply of electricity and assured raw material at minimum cost
qa.e: Smelting uses a lot of electricity and needs a steady, low-cost supply of bauxite.

qa.q: Which fertiliser raw material does India import entirely because it has no commercially usable reserves?
qa.e: India has no commercially usable reserves of potash, so it is entirely imported.

qa.q: The cement industry requires bulky raw materials such as:
qa.e: Cement is made from limestone, silica and gypsum, using coal and electric power.

qa.q: Which city is known as the 'electronic capital of India'?
qa.e: Bengaluru is called the electronic capital of India because of its many electronics and IT industries.

qa.q: How many types of pollution does your textbook say industries cause?
qa.a: Four: air, water, land and noise
qa.e: Industries are responsible for four types of pollution: air, water, land and noise.

qa.q: Thermal pollution of water occurs when:
qa.a: Hot water from factories is drained into rivers before cooling
qa.e: Hot water discharged from factories and thermal plants raises water temperature and harms aquatic life.

qa.q: Which device fitted to smoke stacks helps reduce air pollution?
qa.e: Electrostatic precipitators, fabric filters, scrubbers and inertial separators trap particles from smoke.

qa.q: The secondary stage of treating industrial effluents uses:
qa.e: Primary treatment is mechanical, secondary is biological and tertiary combines biological, chemical and physical processes.

qa.q: Which is a major solid waste from industries?
qa.e: Fly ash, phosphogypsum and iron and steel slag are major industrial solid wastes.

qa.q: Which of these is an effect of noise pollution?
qa.a: Hearing impairment and increased heart rate
qa.e: Noise causes irritation, anger, hearing impairment, increased heart rate and higher blood pressure.

qa.q: Which step helps reduce air pollution from factories?
qa.a: Using oil or gas instead of coal
qa.e: Oil and gas burn more cleanly than coal, reducing smoke.

qa.q: Which of these is a measure taken by NTPC to protect the environment?
qa.a: Maximising ash utilisation and developing green belts
qa.e: NTPC, with ISO 14001 certification, maximises ash utilisation, develops green belts and recycles ash water.

qa.q: The Golden Quadrilateral links which four cities?
qa.e: The six-lane Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Mumbai.

qa.q: The East-West corridor connects:
qa.e: The East-West corridor runs from Silchar in Assam to Porbandar in Gujarat.

qa.q: Which body maintains district roads?
qa.e: District roads connect district headquarters with other places and are maintained by the Zila Parishad.

qa.q: State highways link a state capital with:
qa.e: State highways connect the state capital with the district headquarters and are maintained by the State PWD.

qa.q: In which year was the Border Roads Organisation established?
qa.e: The Border Roads Organisation was established in 1960 to build roads in strategic border areas.

qa.q: Which is an advantage of roadways over railways?
qa.e: Roads give door-to-door service and are economical for short distances and small loads.

qa.q: Metalled roads are made of:
qa.e: Metalled roads use cement, concrete or bitumen (coal tar) and are all-weather roads.

qa.q: Rural roads linking villages with towns got a special boost under which scheme?
qa.e: The Pradhan Mantri Grameen Sadak Yojana focuses on connecting villages with all-weather roads.

qa.q: In which year did the first train in India run from Mumbai to Thane?
qa.e: The first train ran from Mumbai to Thane in 1853.

qa.q: How long was India's first railway journey from Mumbai to Thane?
qa.e: The first train covered a distance of 34 km.

qa.q: Which is the principal mode of transport for freight and passengers in India?
qa.e: Railways are the principal mode of transport for freight and passengers in India.

qa.q: What problems did the Konkan Railway face along the west coast?
qa.e: Building along the hilly, rainy west coast led to sinking tracks and landslides.

qa.q: Which is an advantage of pipelines?
qa.a: Very low running costs and no trans-shipment losses
qa.e: Pipelines are costly to lay but cheap to run, and they avoid losses and delays from shifting goods between vehicles.

qa.q: National Waterway No. 1 is on which river?
qa.e: NW-1 is on the Ganga between Prayagraj (Allahabad) and Haldia.

qa.q: What is the length of National Waterway No. 1 (Prayagraj–Haldia)?
qa.e: NW-1 is 1,620 km long; NW-2 is 891 km and NW-3 is 205 km.

qa.q: National Waterway No. 2 runs between:
qa.e: NW-2 is on the Brahmaputra between Sadiya and Dhubri (891 km).

qa.q: Which was the first port developed soon after Independence?
qa.e: Kandla in Kachchh was developed to ease the load on Mumbai port after Karachi went to Pakistan at Partition.

qa.q: Which port was planned to decongest Mumbai port?
qa.e: Jawaharlal Nehru Port was planned to reduce congestion at Mumbai and serve as a hub port for the region.

qa.q: Which is the premier iron ore exporting port of India?
qa.e: Marmagao in Goa is the premier iron ore exporting port.

qa.q: Which port exports iron ore concentrates from the Kudremukh mines?
qa.e: New Mangalore port in Karnataka handles iron ore concentrates from Kudremukh.

qa.q: Which is the deepest landlocked and well-protected port of India?
qa.e: Visakhapatnam is the deepest landlocked and well-protected port; it was first planned as an outlet for iron ore exports.

qa.q: Why does Kolkata port need constant dredging?
qa.a: It is an inland riverine port on the silt-laden Hugli
qa.e: Kolkata is an inland riverine (tidal) port; the Hugli deposits silt that must be removed regularly.

qa.q: Kochi port is located:
qa.a: At the entrance of a lagoon with a natural harbour
qa.e: Kochi, the extreme south-western port, lies at the entrance of a lagoon with a natural harbour.

qa.q: Pawan Hans Helicopters Ltd provides services to:
qa.a: ONGC's offshore operations and difficult areas like the north-east
qa.e: Pawan Hans helicopters serve ONGC offshore operations and hard-to-reach areas such as the north-eastern states.

qa.q: When a country's imports are more than its exports, its balance of trade is:
qa.e: Imports greater than exports give an unfavourable balance of trade.

qa.q: A country exports goods worth ₹800 crore and imports goods worth ₹600 crore. What is its balance of trade?
qa.e: Exports − imports = 800 − 600 = ₹200 crore; exports are more, so it is favourable.

qa.q: Book packets, registered newspapers and periodicals are sent as:
qa.e: Second-class mail includes book packets, registered newspapers and periodicals, carried by surface mail.

qa.q: Which of these is one of the six mail channels introduced for quick delivery in big cities?
qa.e: The six channels are Rajdhani, Metro, Green, Business, Bulk Mail and Periodical Channels.

qa.q: Trade between two or more countries is called:
qa.e: Trade between countries is international trade; local trade happens within cities, towns and villages, and trade between states is state-level trade.

qa.q: Why is international trade called the 'economic barometer' of a country?
qa.a: Its advancement is an index of the country's economic prosperity
qa.e: Like a barometer measures pressure, the growth of international trade shows how prosperous the economy is.

qa.q: Which body certifies both Indian and foreign films in India?
qa.e: The Central Board of Film Certification is the authority for certifying Indian and foreign films.

qa.q: How does tourism help India?
qa.a: It earns foreign exchange and supports local handicrafts
qa.e: Tourism brings foreign exchange, supports local handicrafts and cultural pursuits, and promotes national integration.
